newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira fairly valued at August levels-Italy's Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Lira fairly valued at August levels-Italy's Fazio.

text.p: Italian central bank governor Antonio Fazio said the lira was fairly valued at its August levels and the economy was highly competitive.

Fazio, interviewed in financial magazine Euromoney, said in order for Italian firms to remain competitive, they would have to rely on cost reductions, efficiency gains and product quality "not on currency depreciation."
The interview, which was given in August, was released by the Bank of Italy ahead of its publication on Wednesday. Euromoney voted Fazio Central Banker of the Year.
Asked if the lira was fairly valued, Fazio said: "Yes. The Italian economy is highly competitive at present, as shown by the excellent performance of the balance of payments on current account."

The lira strengthened from a four-month low of 1,036.70 per mark on August 1 to around 1,020 by the end of the month, although it climbed as high as 1,014 over that period. The lira is currently trading at 1,006.70 to the mark.

Fazio, asked if he believed the central bank had tamed inflationary expectations in Italy, replied: "We have not yet broken the back of inflation: the expected values of price increases are still too high."

"The point I am insisting on is that we have to reject the habit of thinking that prices can only rise. There are prices that can fall, in absolute terms, not just in terms of a reduction in their rate of increase," he said.
He noted July data showed consumer prices falling for the first time in 28 years, adding, "Let us hope for the future."
Six sample Italian cities released preliminary inflation data for September late on Monday showing a provisional year on year rate of 3.4 percent -- flat from the final August rate.

The data disappointed market analysts, who had forecast 3.3 percent, which would have brought the rate closer to the 3.0 percent threshold below which the central bank wants price growth to drop before it lowers interest rates.
Four more cities release data at 1530 GMT on Tuesday and the final figure is due out on October 4. --Milan bureau +392 66129507
